A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original microstructure-generation experiments, simulator-based metamaterial design results, and copyright-constrained generation results, with additional empirical evidence in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports additional copyright-baseline results and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes its stopping criterion from the full violation-plus-distance objective to constraint violation alone. The decoder-based proximal correction, simulator perturbations, and classifier-based correction remain. The expanded augmented-Lagrangian description does not by itself establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: Both evaluate microstructure porosity, metamaterial stress-strain inverse design including interpolation and extrapolation, and Mickey Mouse/Jerry generation using the same datasets. V2 mentions tortuosity in its introduction but documents no additional tortuosity experiment.

E2.justification: V2 adds Projected Diffusion Models to the copyright-generation comparison in Figure 5; v1 Section 6.3 compares against conditional diffusion only. The microstructure and metamaterial comparator sets, including the unsuccessful appendix baselines, remain.

E3.justification: The added copyright PDM comparison uses 64×64 sampling followed by upscaling after unsuccessful 1024×1024 generation, introducing a baseline protocol with different resolution from the latent models. Existing microstructure preprocessing, the 8,000-image copyright dataset, and the ten-perturbation, five-step DPO setting remain.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an efficiency comparison examining correction overhead: conditional versus constrained sampling takes 10 versus 50 seconds for microstructures and 10 versus 65 seconds for copyright generation. Existing structural analyses, extrapolation cases, and correction examples remain; Figure 8 enlarges an existing DPO example.

E5.justification: The existing plus/minus reporting for FID and metamaterial MSE is retained. Neither version specifies experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 5 adds copyright PDM results of 71% constraint satisfaction and 75.3 FID, and Appendix F adds runtime entries. Retained benchmark numbers match, including microstructure FIDs, metamaterial errors and invalid-shape rates, and copyright results for conditional diffusion and the proposed method.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix B offers a short final-projection feasibility argument. V2 retains that argument in Appendix G and adds Theorems 4.1–4.2, non-asymptotic feasibility and KL-divergence bounds, regularity assumptions, and extensive proofs in Appendix H. These substantially expand the mathematical content.

C1.justification: The central training-free constrained-generation contribution remains. V2 corrects the abstract's video-generation framing, explicitly claims almost-sure feasible convergence for convex constraints, and introduces an exact-tortuosity claim in the introduction without a corresponding added experiment.

C2.justification: V1 emphasizes that image-space correction generally differs from latent projection. V2 asserts latent-projector equivalence under smoothness and interprets its new KL bound as preserving sample quality. It also adds substantive limitations concerning image-only demonstrations, deferred guidance comparisons, and computational cost.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents augmented-Lagrangian multiplier and penalty updates with Algorithm 2. Appendix F adds specific GPU/CPU hardware and task-level timings. Existing classifier architecture, Monte Carlo sample count, and DPO runtime information are retained, sometimes relocated.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against constrained latent-diffusion research, including ReSample, Rout et al., Zirvi et al., and CLAD. It also discusses constrained graph and time-series generation and adds optimization foundations, replacing v1's much narrower treatment of neighboring approaches.

P1.justification: The introduction, preliminaries, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. Section 4 is reordered, simulator differentiation moves into the renamed Section 5, related work moves to Appendix B, and limitations, solver details, runtime discussion, and proofs receive dedicated appendices.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column main layout with a single-column format and substantially rearranges figures and algorithms. The copyright figure gains a results table and revised PCA display, a runtime table is added, and the existing DPO illustration receives an enlarged appendix presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 improves comparison coverage, positioning, and technical disclosure, but its major theoretical expansion has material problems. Appendix H.1 uses an invalid inequality that halves a positive remainder, while H.3 requires the training distribution to lie within the feasible set despite Section 4.2 invoking the fidelity bound for experiments that violate that condition. These theoretical weaknesses coexist with concrete documentation and evaluation gains, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
